item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
+ This is what I want to change
- Here they are

however, testing [DATA EXPUNGED] further investigation

It cuts off in the middle of a sentence, so I'd like to change this so that [DATA EXPUNGED] refers to a noun

however, after testing on the "threads", researchers discovered [DATA EXPUNGED], requiring further investigation.

Next is this part

concrete, steel, titanium, carbon fiber, bone, wood, [DATA EXPUNGED]

The expungement implies that the foundation would feed it anomalous items that are on a need to know basis, hence why they expunged it. What reasons would the foundation have to do that, especially if they want to keep the items classified?

concrete, steel, titanium, carbon fiber, bone, wood, and other similar materials that are indigestible to non-anomalous canines.

It ends in a more plausible manner without needing to list everything that the dog eats.
Lastly

In this state, SCP-367 is highly aggressive, and has been observed to [DATA EXPUNGED].

It looks as if the author couldn't think of anything to fill it in.

In this state, SCP-367 is highly aggressive, and has been observed to [DATA EXPUNGED] living organisms, rendering them immobile for later consumption.

This gives readers more of an idea what action 367 is taking is supposed to be.
These are the edits I wish to make, and apologies for the wait, school and all. Thanks for taking this under consideration.

item.content:encoded: No it wouldn't. Because doing something like that is tempting fate, and articles have generally moved away from that direction. Doing a test log going:"We tried to feed its dead progeny to it - but it went berserk and ate researcher X's head" is firmly in the realm of lolFoundation, which is something that generally isn't done anymore outside of -Js and tales.

item.title: Re: Food
item.content:encoded:
Guys, come on, reduce reuse recycle.

For the Foundation, this means "How many Class D have we lost this week? And we've had their autopsies done already, right? Okay, call 367's feed squad and warm up the meat mincer."

We have to be careful around self-replicating SCPs. Those are always, always tricky.

item.title: Re: Food
item.content:encoded:
Guys, come on, reduce reuse recycle.

But this would still make for an interesting test log. Maybe it might multiply more than usual, or it could go berserk at the prospect of eating its brethren.

I'm saying this because I'm the type of person who hoardes all the arrows/one-time-use items in games for when I really need it but never use it. The thought of chemically destroying this thing over and over gets my OCD going.

item.title: Re: Food
item.content:encoded:
How do we know letting them eat eachother's dead bodies wouldn't cause SUPERMASSIVEHYPERACTIVESUDDENMULTIPLICATION?

item.title: Re: Food
item.content:encoded: Still, every bit counts. Really what I'm asking is if we really have to chemically destroy these things or if we could just let them each others dead bodies. It would make feeding a bit easier because it wouldn't run out.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I think there's too much [DATA REDACTED]. It doesn't stir a "Oh my god, what horrors are being concealed?!" reaction in this case, it stirs more of a "Oh my god, the author couldn't actually explain this part!" reaction. But then I have that to [DATA REDACTED] a lot, so maybe it's just me, I'll admit that much.

I'd say either write around these instances so that the redactions are less jarring, or surround the redactions with a tad more info so that it looks more like they're actually concealing something than "and here's where I stopped trying to explain it".

So what wins in a fight in a dark room, a hungry 367 or 363?
